hints.content:
Rutendo is trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the number of bananas per $1$ muffin.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{bananas}}}{\maroonD{\text{muffins}}} = \purpleD{\text{bananas per muffin}}$

If we write each unit rate as a decimal, we can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

Let's see what Rutendo did instead.

###Finding the unit rates

Recipe| $\blueE{\text{Bananas}} $ ||  $\maroonD{\text{Muffins}}$||$\purpleD{\text{Bananas per muffin}}$
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
$A$  |$3$|$\div$ | $12$|$=$|$0.25$
$B$|$5$ |$\div$ |$24$ | $\approx$|$0.21$
$C$ |$11$ |$\div$ | $48$|$\approx$| $0.23$

Rutendo divided the number of muffins by the number of bananas instead. That's a different unit rate than he wanted.

###The mistake

Rutendo calculated muffins per banana instead of bananas per muffin.

question.content:
A baker has three  banana muffin recipes. Recipe A uses $3$ bananas to make $12$ muffins.  Recipe B uses $5$ bananas to make $24$ muffins. Recipe C uses $11$ bananas to make $48$ muffins.

Rutendo tried to order the recipes from least to greatest by *bananas per muffin*, but he made a mistake. Here's his work:

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{12}{3}&=4\\\\
\dfrac{24}{5}&=4.8\\\\
\dfrac{48}{11}&\approx 4.36\\\\
\stackrel{\text{Least}}{\underbrace{4}_\text{Recipe A}} &< \underbrace{4.36}_\text{Recipe C} < \stackrel{\text{Greatest}}{\underbrace{4.8}_\text{Recipe B}}
\end{align}$

**What was Rutendo's mistake?**

[[☃ radio 2]]

choices.content: Rutendo calculated muffins per banana instead of bananas per muffin.
Rutendo ordered by number of muffins instead of by bananas per muffin.
